candidate_relations.reason: Congenital blistering followed by hyperkeratotic plaques and a KRT1 variant establish ichthyosis, but the annular epidermolytic subtype is omitted.
KRT1 p.L161P and suprabasal vacuolization place the disease within keratinopathic ichthyoses without naming the annular phenotype.
Thick brown corrugated plaques represent keratosis, but this finding does not encompass neonatal bullae, epidermolysis, or the KRT1 cause.
The course begins with neonatal vesicles and later annular plaques with epidermolytic histology rather than fixed symmetric erythrokeratodermic plaques.
Palmoplantar hyperkeratosis developed later as one feature of the generalized KRT1 disorder rather than the complete diagnosis.
The later lesions are discrete round or annular plaques, not persistent generalized ichthyosiform erythroderma.
Congenital onset and a heterozygous KRT1 variant prove a genodermatosis, but this class lacks its epidermolytic annular identity.
The pathogenic KRT1 change supports keratinopathy, while the label does not specify ichthyosis, epidermolysis, or annular plaques.
Eruptions persisted for years and progressed to hyperkeratotic plaques, unlike erythema toxicum neonatorum.
Ichthyosis bullosa of Siemens is typically a more superficial KRT2 disorder, whereas this child has a KRT1 variant and granular-to-upper-spinous vacuolization.
Biopsy locates bullae within epidermis with upper spinous and granular vacuolization, not the basal cleavage pattern of epidermolysis bullosa simplex.
No nail dystrophy, oral leukokeratosis, or painful focal keratoderma suggests pachyonychia congenita.
The KRT1-associated evolution from neonatal bullae to annular hyperkeratotic plaques and epidermolytic histology identifies an ichthyosis rather than epidermolysis bullosa.
The lesions are vesiculobullous and plaque-like without follicular papules typical of keratosis pilaris.
Ichthyosis vulgaris does not produce congenital bullae or the marked suprabasal vacuolization seen on biopsy.
Hyperkeratosis with suprabasal vacuolization is epidermolytic hyperkeratosis, but the candidate omits the clinically distinctive annular ichthyosis variant.
Hyperkeratosis is visible in the plaques and on biopsy but is only one component of the inherited blistering ichthyosis.
Normal vital signs, recurrence from birth, and a KRT1 mutation exclude an acute staphylococcal toxin syndrome.
Bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma captures the neonatal blistering epidermolytic ichthyosis spectrum but not the later annular plaque phenotype.
